review_notes: I read the whole file and its direct dependencies in Unitriangular.lean and Vector.lean. I also grepped for downstream uses of the `_left`/`comp_quotient` lemmas. I could not run Lean. The simp-set claims below are judgments about likely effects, not observed simp behaviour. The two `@[simp]` inverse lemmas (`unitriangularStageToGL_fromGL`, `unitriangularStageFromGL_toGL`) look fine: their LHS is a composite and their RHS is a variable. I found no loops or competing rules. I did not recommend simp on the naturality or successor lemmas, because their shapes are less canonical.

findings.excerpt:
(unitriangularStageFromGL K n r R s).comp (quotient K n r) =
      unitriangularFromGL K (Fin n) R s.1
findings.problem: This is the characterising lemma of `unitriangularStageFromGL`, a `liftₐ` definition. It reduces `lift.comp quotient` to the ambient-level `unitriangularFromGL`, so it is the canonical simp lemma for the definition. It is not tagged `@[simp]`. Every proof that mentions it has to be steered by hand with `change` and `rw`. It is rewritten manually seven times in this file (in `unitriangularStageToGL_fromGL`, `unitriangularStageFromGL_toGL`, `unitriangularStageMulEquivAlgHom` twice, `unitriangularStageFromGL_natural` twice, and `unitriangularStageFromGL_successor` twice). It is also used by `rw` in UnitriangularStageCoordinates.lean line 181. Its two inverse partners, `unitriangularStageToGL_fromGL` and `unitriangularStageFromGL_toGL`, are `@[simp]`, so the simp interface for this definition is only half specified.
findings.proposed_change: Mark it `@[simp]`. The LHS `AlgHom.comp (unitriangularStageFromGL ..) (quotient ..)` has a definition head and the RHS is strictly simpler. The only competing rewrite is `AlgHom.comp_assoc`, which is not simp, so I see no loop. Then the `rw [unitriangularStageFromGL_comp_quotient, unitriangularStageFromGL_comp_quotient]` chains can become `simp only [unitriangularStageFromGL_comp_quotient]` or plain `simp`, and they no longer depend on the number of occurrences. If tagging it is thought risky for downstream files, add it to a named simp set instead.
findings.benefit: Users reasoning about points of the stage Hopf quotient get the descended map reduced to the ambient `unitriangularFromGL` automatically. The repeated rewrite chains in the proofs get shorter and less fragile.

findings.excerpt:
theorem unitriangularStagePointMulEquiv_apply_left
    (s : Matrix.UnitriangularGroup.superdiagonalSubgroup n R r) :
    (unitriangularStagePointMulEquiv K n r R s).left =
      Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (unitriangularStageFromGL K n r R s).toRingHom) := rfl
findings.problem: The file has three `.left` unfolding lemmas that are the only API for reading a scheme morphism built from `Spec.map`. They are `unitriangularStageInclusion_left` (line 62), `unitriangularStageSuccessor_left` (line 112) and `unitriangularStagePointMulEquiv_apply_left` (line 224). None is `@[simp]`, so every consumer must name them in `rw`. The proofs of `unitriangularStageSuccessor_point`, `unitriangularStageInclusion_point` and `unitriangularStagePointsIso` all spend `change` and `rw` lines on this. External files do the same (UnitriangularStageCoordinates.lean line 136, line 189). They are also awkward to use because the definitions are `rfl`-level and `.hom.hom.left` is not reducible, so `simp` cannot see through them. The sibling file Vector.lean tags the analogous `vectorGroupMulEquivPoints_apply_left` as `@[simp]`, and VectorProduct.lean does the same for `vectorGroupSchemeMap_left`. So this file departs from the library's own convention.
findings.proposed_change: Tag the three lemmas `@[simp]`, as `vectorGroupMulEquivPoints_apply_left` is. Each RHS is a `Spec.map` of an explicit ring hom, so the RHS is normal form for `Spec.map_comp`/`Spec.map_id` and there is no cycle. Then the combination steps such as `rw [unitriangularStagePointMulEquiv_apply_left, unitriangularStageSuccessor_left, ← Spec.map_comp]` can be driven by `simp only [..]`. If tagging the `.hom.hom.left` lemmas is judged too broad, tag at least `unitriangularStagePointMulEquiv_apply_left`, which matches the Vector precedent exactly.
findings.benefit: Point-level statements get a uniform simp normal form `Spec.map (ofHom ..)`, which matches the existing `vectorGroup…_left` simp lemmas. The commutation proofs shrink, and later files no longer have to rediscover and spell out the lemma names.
